description: Pre-series Concorde 201, MSN 201; used for French presidential flights and displayed inside the main hall. Owned by ANAE.
Air France Concorde MSN 209 on the south apron, repainted in Air France colours in 2015.
MSN 238, Airbus Heritage collection; the cabin is open to visitors.
Airbus outsize-cargo carrier; last flight 15 March 1996 after 14110 hours; moved to Aeroscopia in March 2014 and open to visitors. Owned and maintained by Ailes Anciennes Toulouse.
Airbus collection light business jet in the main hall.
Falcon 10 number 02, used as the Turbomeca Larzac engine testbed; restored by Ailes Anciennes Toulouse and displayed in the main hall.
Flown in from Châteaudun in 1983, then used for teaching at the IUT de Rangueil; recovered in 2014 and now shown in the Aeroscopia hall near the Concorde. Owned by Ailes Anciennes Toulouse.
Second Gazelle prototype; came from the CEAT in 1998 after ground-test use, restored by Ailes Anciennes Toulouse and displayed near the Concorde.

Bare-metal Mirage IIIC of the Ailes Anciennes Toulouse collection. AAT holds two Mirage IIIC (90 in natural metal and 86 in Djibouti Vixen colours); which of the two is inside Aeroscopia needs checking on site.

Came from the CEAT at Toulouse in 1986; restored by Ailes Anciennes Toulouse and repainted in the livery of aircraft number 8 shown at the 1946 Grand Palais salon, a marking it did not originally wear. Now inside Aeroscopia.
Ex-Luftwaffe, from Manching via the German army museum at Koblenz in 1989; first flew 1963 with 3684 flying hours, mostly with JG 34. Ailes Anciennes Toulouse collection.
Obtained from a Czech museum in 1999 in exchange for a Fouga Magister; extensively rebuilt by Ailes Anciennes Toulouse.

First flew 18 February 1959; served with GAEL, EC 10, EC 5, ELA 44, Salon-de-Provence, Chambéry, Mont-de-Marsan and ELA 41; retired 28 April 1997. Ailes Anciennes Toulouse; displayed inside Aeroscopia.

French Navy Crusader displayed with its engine; Ailes Anciennes Toulouse collection. Serial not published by the association. Serial from the ARDHAN inventory of preserved French naval aircraft dated February 2025.

Navy Alouette II, the fifth built and the first fitted with wheels; brought from the Dordogne in May 2005 and fully restored by Ailes Anciennes Toulouse volunteers before going inside Aeroscopia. Serial from the ARDHAN inventory of preserved French naval aircraft dated February 2025.

Serial 0995, painted as a US Air Force O-2A. Wikipedia places it in the Aeroscopia hall while the owning association states it was lent to the neighbouring lycée Saint-Exupéry as a teaching aid; needs checking on site.
Former Météo-France research aircraft flown for the Centre d'Aviation Météorologique from 1987; earlier owned by the Governor of Kentucky. Ailes Anciennes Toulouse collection.
Built 1975-1979 by René Mouliné and flown by him as F-JKHW; given to Ailes Anciennes Toulouse by his family in January 2019.
Amateur-built twin-engine aircraft inspired by the VariViggen; Ailes Anciennes Toulouse collection.
Delivered by Sweden to Austria in 1989, retired from Zeltweg in 2005, arrived dismantled at Toulouse in December 2007; repainted and shown in Aeroscopia since January 2020. Ailes Anciennes Toulouse.
Glider number 117, given to Ailes Anciennes Toulouse in March 2013 and now suspended inside Aeroscopia.
Full-scale replica suspended in the main hall.
Microlight number 208, assembled at Antsirabé in Madagascar in 1999 and originally registered TA-E; flew a Madagascar-to-France raid in 2000-2001. Ailes Anciennes Toulouse.
Amateur-built Gringo recovered from its owner in 2013; suspended inside Aeroscopia.
Flying replica built by Réplic'air, which crossed the Mediterranean in commemoration of Roland Garros; suspended in the hall between flights.
Held by the Airbus Group Foundation and suspended in the main hall. Sub-variant and serial not published.
Amateur-built canard, also called MiniShinden, given to Ailes Anciennes Toulouse by its builder and installed in Aeroscopia in June 2016.
aliases: RC01; RC-01; Spirit of Cavaroc; MiniShinden

description: Electric demonstrator entrusted to Ailes Anciennes Toulouse by Airbus in December 2019; recovered from Saint-Martin-du-Touch and reassembled inside Aeroscopia.
MSN 280, the last Caravelle built; on the south apron in Air Inter colours.
Prototype MSN 001, on the south apron since June 2015. One source says a Transall has since taken its place on that stand; needs checking on site.

Chosen for the C-160 farewell tour of 14 March to 1 April 2022 and painted accordingly; made its last flight into Toulouse-Blagnac on 27 June 2022. Owned by Ailes Anciennes Toulouse and parked on the Aeroscopia apron.
MSN 098, the first ATR 72-600; north apron, opened March 2020.
MSN 360, the first A340-600; north apron.
MSN 001, the first A320, christened by Diana Princess of Wales; north apron.
MSN 002 development aircraft; cockpit and both decks are open to visitors. North apron.
MSN 003, displayed in the livery of MSN 001 and marked F-WEGA, which is not its own registration. North apron.
